summary: Integral module-psi and explicit Herr deformation-retraction checkpoint, with the native degree-1/2 psi complex. Reuses the existing scalar trace/psi supplier and native tensor/cochain/homotopy/homology APIs. The actual coefficient rings, analytic kernel inverse, Galois/Iwasawa comparisons, Wach construction and relative theorem proofs remain separated from this algebraic core.

conventions.scalar: Use two copies R and S and the specified Frobenius algebra map. Do not let an inferred identity self-algebra change the tensor product or trace. Normalized trace is constructed integrally at its scalar owner before p-torsion reduction; trace=0 modulo p does not define psi.
conventions.fixedCoefficients: Herr operators and kernels are linear over a fixed coefficient ring C. Phi/psi need not be linear over the period ring. An algebraic basis does not automatically give continuous coordinates in every weak/annular topology.
conventions.torsion: KPX Delta_K is the p-torsion subgroup, trivial for odd p. The roadmap odd-prime full prime-to-p torsion convention requires a comparison; it is not silently identified with KPX. Rational order-two averaging and integral p=2 derived descent are different.
conventions.signs: d0=((F-1),(G-1)), d1=((G-1),-(F-1)); signed comparison=(id,diag(-psi,id),-psi). The psi complex is in cohomological degrees 1 and 2.
conventions.comparison: F:C_phi→C_psi, S:C_psi→C_phi. In functional notation FS=id and id-SF=dH+Hd. In categorical notation S followed by F is identity, and the homotopy is between id and F followed by S.
conventions.status: All implementationStatus fields are unchecked. Conditional algebra does not instantiate missing arithmetic hypotheses. Suggested signatures are uncompiled.

declarations.provides: Existing balanced tensor-product universal construction as a linear map; use the specified scalar actions, not a second tensor carrier.
Equality of tensor-product maps from equality on pure tensors.
Wrap an actual linear map as a native module-category morphism. Categorical f followed by g represents g composed with f.
Construct a native cochain complex from terms, successive differentials and their zero-composition proof.
Construct a native cochain map from degree maps and commuting squares.
Native chain homotopy with degree-minus-one components and the equation f=dH+Hd+g.
Canonical homology isomorphism induced by a constructed homotopy equivalence.
Native homology as the actual outgoing-map kernel modulo the incoming-map image, with quotient/cycle maps.
Native cycles as the linear-map kernel; the inclusion comparison fixes the map, not just its isomorphism class.

nodes.title: Balanced scalar psi on a tensor product
nodes.statement: Construct the R-linear map psiTensor_r:S tensor_R M→M by s tensor m ↦ r(s)m.
hypotheses: R,S are commutative rings with a specified algebra map R→S. M is an R-module. The action on S is this map, modelling Frobenius, not an inferred identity self-action.
r:S→R is R-linear for that action.
proofSteps: The map is additive in both variables. For a∈R, r(a·s)m=a r(s)m=r(s)(am), so it is balanced.
Apply the existing TensorProduct.lift.
acceptance: Do not invert p. The proof also works for torsion modules M.

nodes.statement: Define psi_N=psiTensor_r composed with L inverse, as an R-linear map N→M. It is integral whenever the actual input rings, r and L are integral.
hypotheses: R,S are commutative, with specified R→S; M is an R-module and r:S→R is R-linear for that map.
N is an S-module with compatible restricted R-action. L:S tensor_R M ≃_S N is the actual Frobenius linearization, not the Galois/module equivalence.
proofSteps: Restrict scalars on L inverse and compose with psiTensor.
Keep source N and target M distinct at a fixed radius; identify them only through the supplied full-ring transition maps.
acceptance: A linearization alone does not supply topology, a stable lattice or a Galois representation.

nodes.statement: An R-linear q:N→M satisfying q(L(s tensor m))=r(s)m for all s,m equals psi_N. Computation in different bases of the same linearized module therefore gives the same operator.

nodes.statement: For R-linear f:M→M′ and S-linear g:N→N′ with g(L(s tensor m))=L′(s tensor f(m)), psi_N′ g=f psi_N.
hypotheses: The two actual linearizations use the same specified R→S and scalar r; all scalar actions are compatible.
proofSteps: On L(s tensor m), both sides equal r(s)f(m).

nodes.title: Semilinear Gamma compatibility
nodes.statement: Let sigma_R,sigma_S commute with R→S, and g_M,g_N be the corresponding semilinear maps. If g_N(L(s tensor m))=L(sigma_S(s) tensor g_M(m)) and r sigma_S=sigma_R r, then psi_N g_N=g_M psi_N.
hypotheses: The actual ring/module/linearization data of linearized-psi, with the stated scalar semilinearity and compatibility equations. No finite-group averaging.
proofSteps: On L(s tensor m), both sides equal sigma_R(r(s))g_M(m).
Use additivity, pure-tensor spanning and surjectivity of L.

nodes.title: Continuity from actual finite coordinates
nodes.statement: Suppose finitely many b_i∈S and continuous c_i:N→M satisfy x=Σ L(b_i tensor c_i(x)). If M is a topological additive group with continuous constant R-scalar multiplication, psi_N is continuous.
hypotheses: The actual algebraic data of linearized-psi; the stated finite reconstruction and coordinate continuity in the claimed topology.
proofSteps: The pure formula gives psi_N(x)=Σ r(b_i)c_i(x).
Every summand is continuous and the sum is finite.
acceptance: Algebraic freeness alone is not continuous coordinates for every weak or annular topology.

nodes.title: Two-term psi complex

Only d(1,2) is nonzero, so consecutive composites vanish.

nodes.title: Functoriality of psi complexes
nodes.statement: For h intertwining psi and psi′, construct the map of psi complexes given by h in degrees 1 and 2 and zero elsewhere.
hypotheses: C-modules M,M′ and C-linear psi,psi′,h with h psi=psi′ h.
proofSteps: The nontrivial square is h(psi-1)=(psi′-1)h.
Identity and composition hold degreewise.

nodes.title: Degree-one psi homology
nodes.statement: The native degree-one homology is canonically isomorphic to ker(psi-id), sending a cycle class to the same vector because there are no incoming boundaries.
hypotheses: C commutative; M a C-module; psi C-linear.
proofSteps: Use the native short complex 0→M→M at degree 1.
Apply moduleCatHomologyIso and quotient by zero; the cycles inclusion fixes the actual map.
acceptance: This is not yet H1_Iw(K,T)=psi-fixed vectors.

proofSteps: Use the native short complex M→M→0 at degree 2.
All of M is cycles; apply the native quotient-by-image identification.
acceptance: Derived specialization can have additional Tor terms; ordinary base change is not asserted.
